RESULT [attribution]: From the HTML version: linear datamodeling score (LDS) for removing 1% / 5% of data on CIFAR-10 ResNet-9 is 0.96 / 0.98 for MAGIC vs 0.24 / 0.07 for TRAK and 0.50 / 0.18 for EK-FAC. On Gemma-2B instruction tuning it is 0.95 / 0.99 vs TRAK 0.06 / 0.13. Cost is about 3-5x one training run per test target. It requires deterministic, 'smooth' training and degrades beyond about 20% data removal.
US [attribution]: This shows that cheap attribution methods correlate only weakly with ground truth for deep nets, so a 'which batch hurt' analyser built on TRAK or influence functions would mostly return noise. MAGIC itself would require deterministic YOLO training (fixed order, no nondeterministic cuDNN, smooth versions of mosaic/augment) and several training runs per target metric. Worth a pilot on one small inc [note truncated at collection]
